title: Jamming with Tatum and Stuff Smith; Sebastian's police arrangement
summary: They jammed all night with clarinet, and Frank Sebastian stayed open late through police payoffs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who all else, what other musicians, were you likely to be playing with (inaudible)?
Well, we used to have a group, we used to jam with Art Tatum. Stuff Smith and I, we used to go out and jam all the time. We'd stay out all night.
Were you playing horn or were you playing (inaudible)?
The clarinet, the clarinet. And we'd go when we got off of work at three o'clock in those days, three

o'clock in the morning, and that's where Sebastian's Cotton Club, got off at three o'clock in the morning. It was out in Culver City and he had a -- Frank Sebastian had a good deal with the police out there. He could sort of do things like he wanted to. When other places would close at two o'clock in the morning, he'd stay open until three, four, and sneak things under the counter and under the tables and all that kind of stuff and he controlled the police department and the sheriff's department in his area there, big pay-off.
How did Louie Armstrong get busted that time then?

He got busted, just ridiculous. Some guy tried to make a -- was trying to make a name for him or something. That's right before I came with the band. I was working downtown, Taxi Dancer (PHONETIC) at the time. That was the first time Louie ever came out here and some guy was -- on the police force was trying to get a pay-off and Louie didn't pay him off, so he busted him.
No, he got to him before Frank could get to it, you know?
Because I've heard that that was some kind of set-up.
Sure, it was a set-up. A set-up to get
some loot from one of them jive cops. Just was trying to get a pay-off.
